title: Wishing to have seen the older Bourbon Street era
summary: Wondering what it was like when clubs were jazz clubs; Rowe mentions Kidd Jordan and Clyde Kerr and studio stories.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: A gig is a gig. You know sometimes I wish — well I don’t necessarily wish that I’d been there during that time, but I wonder what it would have been like to be there at a time when all those clubs on Bourbon Street were jazz clubs. And when a lot of the older musicians that have since passed on, when they were still alive, living, and what their experiences were like, you know what I mean? I hear stories, but it would have been interesting to see what that would have been like to be around those cats.
Yeah. You know I got to talk with a couple of the guys who had come up here, Kidd Jordan.
Clyde, yeah. And they were talking about some of the studio stuff that went on down there and it was just so fascinating.
I hope someone invents a time machine someday, so you can go back.
Right. I mean yeah, that would be cool. I don’t know if I’d actually want to be living there, but I’d like to be aware of what’s happening.
Watch Louis Armstrong being arrested on that evening.
